stories.Headline: India to host 3rd BRICS Culture Working Group meeting in Bhopal on August 5-6
stories.Summary:
India will host the third BRICS Culture Working Group Meeting in Bhopal on August 5-6 as part of its 2026 chairmanship. Representatives from all BRICS member states will participate to promote cultural cooperation and prepare for an upcoming Culture Ministers' Meeting. The discussions will focus on three main areas, including creative economy and industries, cultural heritage protection and repatriation, and connections between culture and sustainable development.

In a separate but related development, India also called for enhanced cooperation among BRICS nations to combat corruption and cross-border crime. A two-day Anti-Corruption Working Group Meeting began in Hyderabad on August 4, which includes sessions on extraditing fugitive offenders, recovering stolen assets, and addressing financial crime. The program features discussions about BRICS cooperation networks and addresses emerging risks from new financial technologies and digital assets.

stories.Headline: Many Irish workers fear their job is under threat from AI
stories.Summary:
A survey by IReach on behalf of NFP Ireland found that only 30% of Irish workers feel their jobs are safe from artificial intelligence and automation over the next decade. Around 40% of respondents believe their overall roles will continue but that individual tasks will likely become automated. Research from ESRI suggested that 7% of current jobs could disappear in the short to medium term.

Younger workers expressed the most concern about job security, with 39% of those aged 18 to 24 saying large parts of their roles could vanish, compared to just 15% of workers over 55. Those aged 35 to 44 felt most confident their jobs could not be replaced by AI. NFP Ireland's managing director noted that while routine tasks will likely become automated, human skills like creativity, communication, and leadership will remain important, and younger workers worry that entry-level positions vulnerable to automation represent crucial stepping stones for career development.

stories.Headline: C-DAC and Geological Survey of India sign Umbrella MoU to Strengthen Geoscience, Mineral Exploration and Disaster Management through Next-Generation Technologies - India Education | Latest Education News | Global Educational News
stories.Summary:
The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, or C-DAC, and the Geological Survey of India, or GSI, signed an agreement on August 4 in New Delhi to work together on mineral exploration and disaster management. The partnership combines C-DAC's advanced computing power with GSI's geological knowledge to tackle complex underground exploration challenges. The organizations will use artificial intelligence and high-performance computing to process large geological data sets and create detailed three-dimensional maps of subsurface areas for mineral targeting.

Beyond exploration, the collaboration will address disaster prevention by monitoring landslides and developing early warning systems for glacier-related floods. The agreement also aims to help India find critical minerals and rare earth elements, which would strengthen the country's economic security and supply chain independence. E Magesh from C-DAC and Pradeep Singh from GSI signed the memorandum in the presence of various government officials from both organizations.

stories.Headline: PalTech Employees Pack 1,000 School Kits for Students Around Hyderabad
stories.Summary:
PalTech employees assembled 1,000 school kits containing notebooks, stationery, and learning supplies over three mornings before work began. These kits are being distributed to underprivileged students in schools around Hyderabad to help them start the new academic year. The company has already begun a second phase to pack an additional 800 kits. A school headmistress praised the initiative for bringing joy to children and providing essential resources they otherwise lack.

The school kit project reflects PalTech's broader commitment to community service, which extends beyond annual campaigns. Earlier initiatives included employee volunteers repainting classrooms at a government school in Nalgonda district and planting trees. The company also sponsored the Run for a Girl Child event supporting girls' education and partnered with Goonj for a clothing distribution drive in rural communities. Company leadership emphasized that these efforts showcase the company's values and employee culture more than the number of items distributed.

stories.Headline: Real IT Solutions Launches AI Advisory Practice to Help West Michigan Businesses Adopt Artificial Intelligence
stories.Summary:
Real IT Solutions, a Grand Rapids managed IT firm, has launched a new AI Business Optimization Services practice to help small and mid-sized businesses in West Michigan adopt artificial intelligence. The company appointed Donald McArthur as Chief AI Officer to lead the effort. McArthur developed proprietary frameworks including the CRAFTED prompting framework, the Hand It Off or Hold On decision model, and an analysis of five hidden costs of AI adoption to guide businesses through structured, risk-aware implementation.

The new practice offers services including AI readiness assessments, tool selection and deployment, Microsoft Copilot integration, workflow automation, and ongoing governance support. Real IT Solutions uses an Assess-Deploy-Sustain methodology to provide businesses with a defined process rather than experimental AI adoption. The company also launched a rebuilt website featuring dedicated service architecture for AI advisory. The firm, founded by CEO Matt Kahle and Chief Technology Officer Adam Peterson, currently serves businesses across Grand Rapids and the broader West Michigan region and maintains a 99.79% client satisfaction score.

stories.Headline: DS Group Leads the Digital Transformation Dialogue in FMCG with ASCEND 2026
stories.Summary:
DS Group, a major Indian consumer goods company, successfully held ASCEND 2026, a three-day technology conference from July 27-29 at its headquarters. The event brought together over 5,000 employees, business leaders, industry experts, and technology partners to discuss how digital technologies are transforming business. The conference showcased applications in artificial intelligence, machine learning, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and other emerging technologies, with major partners like Microsoft, SAP, and Salesforce demonstrating practical business solutions.

Over the past three years, DS Group has doubled its technology investments and expanded its technology partnerships from nearly 20 to over 50 companies. As the company approaches its centenary year, it plans to triple technology investments and aims to become a 20,000 crore rupee organization. The event was conducted as a paperless, digital-first experience to support sustainability goals, reflecting the company's commitment to using technology for both operational efficiency and responsible growth while positioning itself as a leader in digital transformation within the FMCG industry.

stories.Headline: Sneak Peek At New Ride At Ulster County Fair In New Paltz
stories.Summary:
The Ulster County Fair in New Paltz is running from August 4 through August 9, 2026, and celebrating its 138th year as a community tradition. The fair offers typical attractions including farm animals, carnival games, fair food, and fresh squeezed lemonade, along with live entertainment, fireworks, and daily aquatic shows featuring mermaids. Unique events include a Tractor Pull and Corn Shucking Contest.

This year, the fair is introducing a new artificial intelligence powered ride, marking its premiere at the Ulster County Fair. The ride was built by Technical Park of Italy and is the first traveling version of its kind in the United States. Dreamland Amusements, which operates the ride, has highlighted this as an exciting new attraction for Hudson Valley residents to experience at the fair this summer.

stories.Headline: Wildfire and Emergency Response Drones Are Reshaping a Billion-Dollar Market
stories.Summary:
Wildfires are becoming more frequent and intense, prompting emergency response agencies to adopt drone technology as essential tools rather than optional equipment. Drones equipped with thermal imaging and artificial intelligence can detect fire outbreaks, monitor fire movement, and provide real-time video feeds to command centers while operating continuously, even at night when traditional aircraft cannot fly. The firefighting drone market is projected to grow from approximately $2.5 billion currently to over $8 billion by 2032, with the broader emergency management and disaster response market expected to exceed $250 billion in the early 2030s.

Beyond wildfire management, drones are being deployed for hurricane damage assessment, flood monitoring, search and rescue operations, and infrastructure inspection after disasters. Companies like ZenaTech are developing innovative solutions, including acoustic fire suppression technology mounted on autonomous drones that can work in coordinated swarms. Multiple major corporations including Lockheed Martin, PG&E, and Salesforce have launched EMBERPOINT to integrate next-generation wildfire solutions. Governments are significantly increasing investments in these technologies to enhance response efficiency, reduce costs, and protect lives.
